ai.literal: The sweet words of those wearing select bracelets, who do not desire out of love but desire wealth, will bring ruin.
ai.translation: The sweet words of women adorned with choice bracelets, who desire only wealth and not love, will bring ruin.
ai.modern: அன்பினால் விரும்பாமல், பொருளை மட்டுமே விரும்புகின்ற, சிறந்த வளையல்களை அணிந்த பொதுமகளிரின் இன்சொற்கள் ஒருவனுக்கு அழிவைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deceptive sweet talk of courtesans, referred to here as those wearing select bracelets (ஆய்தொடியார்). The poet explains that these women do not act out of genuine love (அன்பின் விழையார்) but are motivated solely by money (பொருள் விழையும்). Therefore, their pleasant and flattering words (இன்சொல்) are untrustworthy and will ultimately lead a person to ruin or disgrace (இழுக்கு தரும்).

ai.literal: Gain weighing, affection speaking, of the character women, benefit weighing, without befriending, should leave.
ai.translation: One should evaluate the true worth of women who speak of affection only after calculating their material gain, and leave them without forming any friendship.
ai.modern: கிடைக்கும் பயனை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்துப் பிறகு அன்பாகப் பேசும் குணம் கொண்ட பொதுமகளிரின் உண்மைத் தன்மையை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து, அவர்களோடு நட்பு கொள்ளாமல் விலகிவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against associating with mercenary women who simulate affection solely for material gain. The poet describes them as those who first calculate the profit ('payan tūkki') and only then speak words of love or virtue ('paṇpu uraikkum'). A wise person must carefully evaluate the true nature and consequences of such relationships ('nayan tūkki') and completely avoid befriending them ('naḷḷā viṭal'). The repetition of the verb 'tūkki' (weighing or evaluating) highlights the contrast between their cold calculation of profit and the wise person's careful evaluation of character.

ai.literal: The false embrace of women who desire wealth is like embracing a stranger's corpse in a dark room.
ai.translation: The false embrace of women who love only wealth is like holding a stranger's corpse in a dark room.
ai.modern: பொருளையே விரும்பும் பொதுமகளிரின் பொய்யான தழுவல், இருண்ட அறையில் அடையாளம் தெரியாத ஒரு பிணத்தைத் தழுவுவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against seeking the company of women who sell their intimacy for money. The poet compares their false, loveless embrace ('பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம்') to holding a cold, lifeless corpse ('பிணம்') of an unrelated stranger ('ஏதில்') in a pitch-black room. Just as a corpse has no warmth, soul, or genuine response, the intimacy of these women is entirely transactional and devoid of real human affection. The imagery of the dark room emphasizes the ignorance, blindness, and spiritual danger of those who indulge in such relationships.

ai.literal: Those who value the true substance will not embrace the mean pleasure, [as do] those of wisdom who seek the wealth of grace.
ai.translation: Those who value the true substance of life and those of wisdom who seek the wealth of grace will never embrace the mean pleasure of prostitutes.
ai.modern: உண்மையான நற்பண்புகளை மதிப்போரும், அருளாகிய உயர்ந்த செல்வத்தை ஆராயும் அறிவுடையோரும், விலைமகளிரின் இழிவான இன்பத்தைப் பொருந்த மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that individuals with true wisdom and moral clarity will not fall for the mercenary affection of prostitutes. The poet uses the term 'punnalam' (mean or worthless pleasure) to describe the superficial intimacy bought with money, which lacks genuine love. Those who value 'poruḷ' (the true substance or virtue of life) and those who seek 'aruṭporuḷ' (the wealth of grace) possess a refined understanding that naturally guards them against such degrading traps. True intellectual and spiritual maturity elevates a person above base, commercialized lust.

ai.literal: Those of common beauty's lowly pleasure will not embrace, by the excellence of their intellect, those of glorious wisdom.
ai.translation: Those who possess glorious wisdom, arising from an excellent intellect, will not embrace the lowly pleasure offered by women of public beauty.
ai.modern: இயற்கையான அறிவு நுட்பத்தால் சிறந்த அறிவைப் பெற்றவர்கள், பொதுவான அழகை விற்கும் மகளிரின் இழிவான இன்பத்தைப் பொருந்த மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the company of public women, referred to here as 'potunalamttār' (those whose beauty is common or public). The poet explains that those who possess 'māṇṭa aṟiviṉavar' (glorious wisdom) which is sharpened by 'matinalam' (excellence of intellect) will never seek 'punnalam' (lowly or worthless pleasure). The word 'punnalam' combines 'pul' (lowly/worthless) and 'nalam' (pleasure/benefit) to describe the fleeting, commercial nature of such relationships. True wisdom guides a person to recognize the emptiness of such pursuits and avoid them entirely.

ai.literal: Those who cherish their own well-being will not embrace, proud of their beauty, those who display cheap pleasure, the shoulders.
ai.translation: Those who cherish their own virtue and well-being will not embrace the shoulders of women who, proud of their physical charm, display and sell their cheap, worthless pleasures.
ai.modern: தங்கள் நன்மையை விரும்புபவர்கள், அழகுச் செருக்குடன் தங்களின் மலிவான இன்பத்தை விற்கும் பொதுமகளிரின் தோள்களைத் தீண்டமாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns self-respecting individuals against associating with prostitutes. The author contrasts two groups: those who cherish their own true well-being ('தந்நலம் பாரிப்பார்') and those who merely trade in cheap, superficial pleasure ('புன்னலம் பாரிப்பார்'). The word 'தகைசெருக்கி' highlights how these women are proud of their outward beauty, which they use to lure others. By choosing not to touch their shoulders ('தோயார் தோள்'), wise people protect their character and dignity from being ruined by temporary, commercialized lust.

ai.literal: Those who lack a mind of integrity will embrace the shoulders of those who physically unite while cherishing [others] in their other mind.
ai.translation: Only those who lack self-control and strength of mind will embrace the shoulders of women who physically unite with them while their hearts cherish someone else.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சுறுதி இல்லாதவர்களே, மனதால் வேறு ஒருவரை நினைத்துக் கொண்டு உடலால் மட்டும் தழுவும் பொதுமகளிரின் தோள்களைச் சேருவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deceit of casual courtesans who sell their affection. The poet explains that these women do not offer genuine love; while they physically embrace a man, their minds are elsewhere, focused on money or other men ('பிறநெஞ்சிற் பேணி'). Only men who lack wisdom and self-control ('நிறைநெஞ்சம் இல்லவர்') will fall for such superficial physical union ('தோள் தோய்வார்'). The key contrast is between the 'full/steadfast mind' (நிறைநெஞ்சம்) that a wise man should possess, and the 'divided/alienated mind' (பிறநெஞ்சு) of the courtesan.

ai.literal: To those who are not of examining wisdom, a tormenting spirit, they say, is the embrace of deceitful women.
ai.translation: The embrace of deceitful women is said to be like a tormenting demoness to those who lack discerning wisdom.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கும் அறிவு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, வஞ்சக குணமுடைய பொதுமகளிரின் தழுவல் வருத்துகின்ற அணங்கு (பேய்) என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the physical allure of deceitful women by comparing their embrace to a tormenting spirit ('அணங்கு'). The word 'அணங்கு' refers to a malevolent deity or demoness that possesses and destroys a person from within. The poet emphasizes that only those who lack discerning wisdom ('ஆயும் அறிவினர் அல்லார்') fall prey to this illusion. For such people, what seems like a pleasurable embrace ('முயக்கு') is actually a destructive force that ruins their life.

ai.literal: The soft shoulders of excellently jeweled women who have no restraint are the deep mire in which base people without nobility sink.
ai.translation: The soft shoulders of beautifully jeweled women who lack moral restraint are a deep mire in which ignoble men sink.
ai.modern: வரையறை இல்லாத, சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த பெண்களின் மென்மையான தோள்கள், மேன்மை இல்லாத கீழ்மக்கள் மூழ்கிக் கிடக்கும் நரகமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the allure of women who sell themselves without any moral restraint or commitment. The poet describes their soft, beautifully adorned shoulders not as a place of pleasure, but as a deep, muddy hell or mire (அளறு) where base, unprincipled men (பூரியர்கள்) sink and lose themselves. The word 'வரைவு' refers to restraint or marriage, indicating women who are not bound by marital fidelity or moral limits. The word 'அளறு' literally means mud or mire, and by extension, hell, emphasizing the inescapable ruin that awaits those who yield to such lust.

ai.literal: Double-minded women, and liquor, and gambling, are the association of those who are abandoned by Fortune.
ai.translation: Association with double-minded women, liquor, and gambling is sought only by those who have been abandoned by Fortune.
ai.modern: இருவேறு மனங்களை உடைய பொதுமகளிர், மது, சூதாட்டம் ஆகிய மூன்றும், திருமகளால் கைவிடப்பட்டவர்களின் சேர்க்கை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against three major self-destructive vices: associating with deceitful women, consuming alcohol, and gambling. The word 'irumana' (double-minded) refers to women who pretend to love for money while harboring different thoughts. The poet states that these three vices are the companions of those who have been forsaken by 'Tiru' (the goddess of fortune or prosperity). Engaging in these habits is both a sign of ruin and the ultimate cause of losing all wealth and grace.
